chapter: Rockwell: Los Angeles club and sessions
title: Memorable moments: Dixieland Jubilee and Slow Drag's bottle bass
summary: Rockwell recalls first seeing the band in tuxedos at the Dixieland Jubilee and Pavageau playing bass on a bottle.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: What about, um... Now, do you have any sort of special memories or outstanding occurrences, memorable moments, or anything like that? Anything that... See, one of the problems about this whole period for me in the... in the 50s is that the band was just sort of... out probably around the different places in the same band, doing more or less the same things, and if there's anything, you know, that stands out or anything of any particular interest?

Well, I remember prior to this time, the first time I saw them, they were at the Dixieland Jubilee, and they came out with tuxedos. And I think they were playing Bourbon Street Parade, Let's Fly Now, and I'll prowl right now down to New Orleans and all. They had these black and white tuxedos, you know, the black tuxedos, and the black tie and the white shirts, and they just looked tremendous, you know, and they just started going, you know. And they just... to me, they just wiped out the whole... Of course, you don't have the intimacy at a concert like that, but...
This was at the Dixieland Jubilee?

Yeah, this is... This was Shrine Bull, Frank Bull. Shrine Auditorium, that's right. But as far as at the caverns, and particularly when I was playing... I do remember this one time when he... I guess he's done it in New Orleans, when Drag was playing bass on a beer bottle, you know, and it was a juice box, and he'd kind of play it against the wall and get a string bass sound out of it. It was a wild...
The last time I was here in New Orleans, he showed me how he did it again at Buster's, and I still can't remember. Were you there when he did that?
He dropped it or something. He dropped it again. He dropped it again.

He dropped it again. He dropped it again. He dropped it again. He dropped it again. It was just wild. It was just wild, and it sounded so much like a string bass. And we used to go over... they were staying at the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel on Hollywood Boulevard, and we would go there after the band and close, and at that time it was a little unusual for a white, young kid to walk in with all these old colored musicians, you know. And I used to just have a ball. We'd sit there and drag it over a suit, and three or four of the musicians would be there, kind of unwinding.
